primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autoimmune T-cell-mediated destruction of pancreatic beta cells causes absolute insulin deficiency and low endogenous C-peptide production.
vignette: A 13-year-old boy has polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, fasting hyperglycemia, and positive islet autoantibodies. Serum C-peptide is low.
lead: Which cell population is primarily destroyed?
distractor_notes: Alpha cells produce glucagon and are not the primary autoimmune target in type 1 diabetes.
Zona glomerulosa cells produce aldosterone and are unrelated to insulin deficiency.
Thyroid follicular-cell destruction causes hypothyroidism rather than diabetes.
Pituitary corticotroph loss causes secondary adrenal insufficiency, not hyperglycemia with islet autoantibodies.
key_expl: Type 1 diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells.
objective: Connect low C-peptide and islet autoimmunity with beta-cell destruction in type 1 diabetes.
clues: weight loss with polyuria and polydipsia

sources.title: Type 1 Diabetes
sources.support: NIDDK describes type 1 diabetes as autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells resulting in little or no insulin production.

sources.title: Type 1 diabetes
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes type 1 diabetes as an autoimmune disease that destroys insulin-producing pancreatic cells.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: TSH-receptor-stimulating autoantibodies activate thyroid follicular cells, causing diffuse thyroid hyperfunction and sometimes autoimmune orbitopathy.
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has weight loss, heat intolerance, palpitations, diffuse goiter, and bilateral proptosis. TSH is suppressed and free T4 is elevated.
distractor_notes: Toxic multinodular goiter causes autonomous thyroid nodules but does not typically produce diffuse autoimmune orbitopathy in a young adult.
Subacute thyroiditis usually causes a painful tender thyroid and transient hormone release rather than proptosis and diffuse stimulation.
Hashimoto thyroiditis most often causes hypothyroidism rather than marked hyperthyroidism with proptosis.
A TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma would produce inappropriately normal or elevated TSH rather than suppressed TSH.
key_expl: Diffuse goiter, hyperthyroidism, suppressed TSH, and proptosis strongly indicate Graves disease.
objective: Diagnose Graves disease from diffuse autoimmune hyperthyroidism with orbitopathy.
clues: suppressed TSH with elevated free T4

sources.title: Graves' Disease
sources.support: NIDDK describes Graves disease as autoimmune hyperthyroidism caused by antibodies that stimulate the thyroid and may cause eye disease.

sources.title: Graves disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes Graves disease as autoimmune hyperthyroidism with goiter and possible eye manifestations.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of thyroid tissue with thyroid autoantibodies gradually reduces thyroid hormone production, producing primary hypothyroidism.
vignette: A 46-year-old woman has fatigue, weight gain, constipation, cold intolerance, and a painless enlarged thyroid. TSH is elevated, free T4 is low, and anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are present.
distractor_notes: Graves disease causes hyperthyroidism with suppressed TSH, not primary hypothyroidism with anti-TPO antibodies.
Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis is typically painful and often follows a viral illness.
Pituitary hypothyroidism produces low or inappropriately normal TSH rather than elevated TSH.
A toxic adenoma causes autonomous hyperthyroidism and suppressed TSH.
key_expl: Primary hypothyroidism with a painless goiter and anti-TPO antibodies is classic Hashimoto thyroiditis.
objective: Recognize Hashimoto thyroiditis from autoimmune primary hypothyroidism and anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies.
clues: high TSH, low free T4, and anti-TPO antibodies

sources.title: Hashimoto's Disease
sources.support: NIDDK describes Hashimoto disease as autoimmune thyroid injury causing hypothyroidism and thyroid autoantibodies.

sources.title: Hashimoto disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes Hashimoto disease as autoimmune inflammation that damages the thyroid and lowers hormone production.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Primary adrenal cortical failure lowers cortisol and often aldosterone; loss of cortisol negative feedback raises ACTH, and mineralocorticoid deficiency causes sodium loss and potassium retention.
vignette: A 39-year-old woman has progressive fatigue, weight loss, hypotension, diffuse hyperpigmentation, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Morning cortisol is markedly low.
distractor_notes: Secondary adrenal insufficiency has low ACTH, typically lacks hyperpigmentation, and generally preserves aldosterone.
Primary hyperaldosteronism causes hypertension and hypokalemia, the opposite mineralocorticoid pattern.
Cushing syndrome causes cortisol excess rather than cortisol deficiency.
SIADH can cause hyponatremia but does not explain hyperkalemia, hyperpigmentation, and low cortisol.
key_expl: Hypotension, hyperpigmentation, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and low cortisol indicate primary adrenal cortical failure.
objective: Differentiate primary adrenal insufficiency from secondary adrenal disease using mineralocorticoid status and ACTH-related hyperpigmentation.
clues: hyponatremia plus hyperkalemia with low cortisol

sources.title: Adrenal Insufficiency & Addison's Disease
sources.support: NIDDK describes primary adrenal insufficiency as deficiency of adrenal hormones with low blood pressure, electrolyte abnormalities, and increased ACTH-related skin darkening.

sources.title: Addison disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes Addison disease as adrenal hormone deficiency causing fatigue, low blood pressure, hyperpigmentation, and electrolyte abnormalities.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: An ACTH-secreting pituitary corticotroph adenoma chronically stimulates the adrenal cortex to produce excess cortisol.
vignette: A 38-year-old woman has central obesity, proximal muscle weakness, purple abdominal striae, hypertension, and hyperglycemia. Cortisol and ACTH are elevated, and MRI shows a pituitary adenoma.
lead: Which sequence best explains the endocrine abnormality?
correct: Pituitary ACTH excess followed by adrenal cortisol excess
distractors: Adrenal cortisol excess followed by increased pituitary ACTH
Hypothalamic CRH deficiency followed by cortisol excess
Aldosterone excess followed by pituitary ACTH excess
Thyroid hormone excess followed by cortisol excess
distractor_notes: Primary adrenal cortisol excess suppresses pituitary ACTH by negative feedback rather than increasing it.
CRH deficiency would lower ACTH and cortisol.
Aldosterone does not drive pituitary ACTH secretion.
Thyroid hormone excess is not the causal axis in Cushing disease.
key_expl: Cushing disease specifically refers to a pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma that drives adrenal cortisol excess.
objective: Distinguish Cushing disease from other causes of Cushing syndrome by identifying pituitary ACTH excess as the initiating lesion.

sources.title: Cushing's Syndrome
sources.support: NIDDK describes Cushing disease as a pituitary tumor that produces excess ACTH and stimulates adrenal cortisol production.

sources.title: Cushing syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes cortisol excess and identifies ACTH-producing pituitary tumors as a cause.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Excess PTH increases bone resorption and renal calcium retention while reducing proximal tubular phosphate reabsorption and increasing calcitriol production.
vignette: A 58-year-old woman has recurrent calcium kidney stones and low bone density. Serum calcium is elevated, phosphate is low, and PTH is elevated.
lead: Which renal effect of PTH directly contributes to the low serum phosphate?
distractors: Inhibition of renal vitamin D activation
distractor_notes: PTH lowers rather than raises proximal phosphate reabsorption.
PTH increases calcium reabsorption in the distal nephron rather than decreasing it.
PTH stimulates renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase and calcitriol production rather than inhibiting vitamin D activation.
PTH increases urinary phosphate excretion rather than suppressing it.
key_expl: PTH promotes phosphaturia by decreasing proximal tubular phosphate reabsorption.
objective: Explain hypophosphatemia in hyperparathyroidism through PTH-mediated phosphaturia.

sources.title: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
sources.locator: Effects of PTH on calcium and phosphorus
sources.support: NIDDK describes excess PTH as raising blood calcium and altering kidney handling of calcium and phosphorus.

sources.title: Hyperparathyroidism
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes PTH effects on bones and kidneys and the hypercalcemia associated with hyperparathyroidism.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: CYP21A2 deficiency blocks cortisol and often aldosterone synthesis, increasing ACTH and shunting steroid precursors toward adrenal androgen production.
vignette: A newborn has ambiguous external genitalia, vomiting, dehydration, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
distractor_notes: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causes androgen excess but also accumulation of deoxycorticosterone with hypertension rather than salt wasting.
17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency reduces sex-steroid production and causes hypertension with hypokalemia.
Aromatase deficiency impairs estrogen synthesis but does not cause the classic salt-wasting CAH pattern with elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone.
5-alpha-reductase deficiency affects conversion of testosterone to DHT and does not cause adrenal salt wasting.
key_expl: 21-hydroxylase deficiency is the most common CAH and causes cortisol deficiency, possible aldosterone deficiency, androgen excess, and elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone.
objective: Identify 21-hydroxylase deficiency from salt-wasting adrenal insufficiency plus androgen excess.
clues: hyponatremia and hyperkalemia in a newborn

sources.title: 21-hydroxylase deficiency
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes CYP21A2 deficiency as causing impaired cortisol synthesis, variable aldosterone deficiency, and excess androgen production.

sources.title: CYP21A2 gene
sources.support: CYP21A2 encodes 21-hydroxylase, an enzyme required in adrenal cortisol and aldosterone synthesis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Complete or partial monosomy X causes ovarian dysgenesis, short stature, and characteristic cardiovascular and lymphatic developmental abnormalities.
vignette: A 15-year-old girl has short stature, webbed neck, primary amenorrhea, and a history of repaired coarctation of the aorta.
distractor_notes: 47,XXY causes Klinefelter syndrome in phenotypic males.
47,XXX causes trisomy X and does not produce the classic Turner phenotype.
47,XYY occurs in males and is not associated with gonadal dysgenesis of Turner syndrome.
46,XY is a typical male karyotype and would not explain the classic Turner findings.
key_expl: Classic Turner syndrome is caused by complete monosomy X, 45,X, although mosaic and structural variants also occur.
objective: Associate short stature, gonadal dysgenesis, and coarctation with monosomy X.

sources.title: Turner syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Turner syndrome as loss or alteration of one X chromosome with short stature and ovarian and cardiovascular abnormalities.

sources.title: Turner Syndrome
sources.support: NICHD describes Turner syndrome as a sex-chromosome disorder involving a missing or structurally altered X chromosome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: An extra X chromosome in a male causes seminiferous tubule dysgenesis, testicular failure, elevated gonadotropins, infertility, and variable gynecomastia.
vignette: A 20-year-old man has tall stature, small firm testes, sparse facial hair, gynecomastia, and infertility.
lead: Which chromosomal complement is most likely?
distractor_notes: 45,X causes Turner syndrome in phenotypic females.
47,XYY is a male sex-chromosome aneuploidy but does not classically produce small testes and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.
46,XX is the typical female chromosomal complement.
47,XXX occurs in females.
key_expl: Klinefelter syndrome most commonly results from an extra X chromosome, yielding 47,XXY.
objective: Recognize Klinefelter syndrome and its characteristic 47,XXY karyotype.

sources.title: Klinefelter syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Klinefelter syndrome as an extra X chromosome in males with testicular dysfunction, infertility, and characteristic physical features.

sources.title: Klinefelter Syndrome
sources.support: NICHD describes Klinefelter syndrome as usually 47,XXY and associated with testicular insufficiency and infertility.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Ovarian hyperandrogenism and disordered follicular maturation produce chronic anovulation; insulin resistance can amplify androgen production and lower sex hormone-binding globulin.
vignette: A 24-year-old woman has irregular menses, acne, hirsutism, obesity, and biochemical evidence of hyperandrogenism.
lead: Which reproductive abnormality most directly explains her irregular menstrual cycles?
correct: Chronic anovulation due to disordered follicular maturation
distractors: Premature depletion of all ovarian follicles
Complete loss of pituitary gonadotropin secretion
distractor_notes: Premature ovarian insufficiency causes low ovarian hormone production and high gonadotropins rather than hyperandrogenism.
Loss of pituitary gonadotropins causes hypogonadotropic amenorrhea and low sex-steroid production.
Cervical obstruction does not cause the endocrine features of hirsutism and hyperandrogenism.
PCOS is characterized by excess, not absent, androgen production.
key_expl: PCOS commonly causes chronic anovulation from abnormal follicular development in a hyperandrogenic metabolic environment.
objective: Explain oligomenorrhea in PCOS through chronic anovulation associated with hyperandrogenism and insulin resistance.

sources.title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
sources.support: NICHD describes PCOS as involving hormonal imbalance, hyperandrogenism, and irregular or absent ovulation.

sources.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes irregular periods, androgen excess, and metabolic abnormalities in PCOS.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Hypothalamic dopamine tonically inhibits prolactin secretion through D2 receptors; loss of dopaminergic restraint or autonomous lactotroph secretion raises prolactin and suppresses GnRH.
vignette: A 31-year-old woman has amenorrhea and galactorrhea. Pregnancy testing is negative. Serum prolactin is markedly elevated, and MRI shows a pituitary microadenoma.
lead: Which hypothalamic neurotransmitter normally inhibits secretion of the elevated hormone?
distractor_notes: Serotonin can influence prolactin regulation but is not the principal tonic inhibitory signal.
Acetylcholine is not the dominant hypothalamic inhibitor of prolactin.
Glutamate is a major excitatory neurotransmitter but does not provide the key tonic inhibition of lactotrophs.
Norepinephrine is not the primary prolactin-inhibiting factor.
key_expl: Dopamine from the hypothalamus tonically inhibits prolactin release through pituitary D2 receptors.
objective: Recall dopaminergic inhibition of prolactin secretion and its physiologic role in hyperprolactinemia.

sources.title: Prolactinoma
sources.support: NIDDK describes prolactinoma as a prolactin-secreting pituitary tumor and dopamine as a major regulator used therapeutically through dopamine agonists.

sources.title: Prolactinoma
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes prolactinoma as a pituitary tumor causing excess prolactin, galactorrhea, and reproductive dysfunction.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Germline activating RET variants constitutively stimulate a receptor tyrosine kinase, predisposing to medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma.
vignette: A 24-year-old woman has medullary thyroid carcinoma and a pheochromocytoma. Several relatives have had similar tumors.
lead: Which molecular abnormality is most likely?
distractors: Biallelic loss of RB1 in all somatic cells
distractor_notes: MEN1 loss causes multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1, typically involving parathyroid, pancreatic endocrine, and pituitary tumors.
Hereditary retinoblastoma involves a germline RB1 variant followed by somatic second hits, not universal biallelic loss in all somatic cells.
CFTR loss causes cystic fibrosis.
HTT CAG expansion causes Huntington disease.
key_expl: MEN2 is caused by germline activating variants in the RET proto-oncogene.
objective: Associate medullary thyroid carcinoma plus pheochromocytoma with activating RET mutations in MEN2.
clues: pheochromocytoma with autosomal dominant family history

sources.title: Multiple endocrine neoplasia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes MEN2 as an inherited tumor syndrome caused by activating RET variants.

sources.title: RET gene
sources.support: RET encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase; activating variants cause constitutive growth signaling and MEN2.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss-of-function androgen receptor variants prevent cellular responses to testosterone and dihydrotestosterone in an XY individual despite normal anti-Müllerian hormone production.
vignette: A 16-year-old phenotypic girl has primary amenorrhea. Breast development is normal, pubic hair is sparse, the vagina ends blindly, and no uterus is seen on ultrasound. Karyotype is 46,XY.
lead: Which molecular defect best explains this phenotype?
distractor_notes: Loss of anti-Müllerian hormone in an XY individual would permit persistence of Müllerian structures such as uterus and fallopian tubes.
21-hydroxylase deficiency affects adrenal steroid synthesis and can virilize XX infants but does not produce this 46,XY pattern with absent uterus.
Aromatase deficiency impairs estrogen synthesis and would not produce normal breast development.
FSH receptor activation is not the mechanism of androgen insensitivity syndrome.
key_expl: Complete androgen insensitivity results from androgen receptor loss of function; testes still produce AMH, so Müllerian structures are absent, while peripheral aromatization supports breast development.
objective: Explain the phenotype of complete androgen insensitivity syndrome using androgen receptor failure with preserved anti-Müllerian hormone action.
clues: normal breasts but sparse pubic hair

sources.title: Androgen insensitivity syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes androgen insensitivity as AR-related failure to respond to androgens in individuals with an XY karyotype.

sources.title: AR gene
sources.support: AR encodes the androgen receptor that mediates cellular responses to testosterone and dihydrotestosterone.
